articles.headline: Two Room-Temperature Antiferromagnetic Semiconductor Candidates

Antiferromagnets have neighboring atomic magnets that point opposite ways and exactly cancel out magnetically. There is an intense drive in computer memory research to create materials in between these two extremes. This post details how a team of AI agents designed a candidate magnet for next-generation computer memory that has zero net magnetism yet still sorts electrons by spin.

articles.headline: Controlling the brain with light earns a physiology Nobel
articles.blurb: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel have won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for their contributions to the field of optogenetics. Optogenetics involves using light to alter the behavior of nerve cells marked by the activity of individual genes. It allows researchers to activate or shut down neurons in an otherwise intact brain. The technique has revolutionized scientists' ability to understand what different populations of nerve cells are doing.

articles.headline: A New Crop of Solar Panels Is the US' Best Hope of Catching China
articles.blurb: Tandem solar is a new technology that adds second and third layers of material on solar panels to convert more of the Sun's radiance into electricity. Several companies plan to start selling panels commercially soon. The panels can generate 25% more energy than current available devices. Successful adoption of the technology will allow the world to meet the rapidly rising demand for electricity with less land and roof area.

articles.headline: Ephemeral testing
articles.blurb: Ephemeral testing is when you test a base application layer by building on top of it. The original work is not assessed - the software built on top of it is. It is a form of integration testing, except the software on top is thrown away when the test is complete. Instead of building the core while trying to anticipate what might be needed at the other layers, you just simulate the other layers by building them.

articles.headline: Why Plain Text Is Still One of the Best Technologies We Have
articles.blurb: The simplicity of plain text is a large part of why it has lasted. Plain text is part of the basic plumbing of computing. There is an enormous collection of tools that know how to work with plain text, and plain text gives users more choice. Text ages surprisingly well, and it is easy to own. It is portable, inspectable, searchable, scriptable, easy to back up, and remarkably resistant to obsolescence.

Rather than appointing a new chief design officer, Apple has Molly Anderson leading industrial design and Steve Lemay leading human interface design, with Ternus acting as the overarching decision-maker. articles.headline: Training AI to Paint with Code
articles.blurb: A language model was trained with reinforcement learning to create watercolor images by writing editable p5.brush JavaScript rather than generating fixed image files, giving people direct control over the resulting artifact. Early training exposed problems with overly complex reward systems, while switching from absolute scores to pairwise comparisons against a hand-rated reference pool produced better images with dramatically shorter code. The experiment shows that applying reinforcement learning to creative work is fundamentally a design problem: subjective qualities like taste need carefully constructed reward structures that provide direction without forcing the model toward a single aesthetic.

articles.headline: 10 Uncomfortable UX Lessons from Real Design Mistakes

Minimalism failed on an ERP shipment form, and a standard landing page beat an artistic, scroll-snapping one in an A/B test. Other lessons favor preventing errors over recovering from them, and giving users an opt-out instead of forcing AI into manual workflows.

Nine principles, refined by 124 people at Services Week 2026, hold that a prototype answers a question, is tested with future users, and can be archived. The tools have changed, with AI-assisted ones now in the mix, but the purpose and principles of prototyping have not.

articles.headline: CFTC proposes new federal framework for leveraged retail crypto trading
articles.blurb: The CFTC launched a rulemaking to create a federal pathway for leveraged and margined retail crypto trading through proposed Regulation CTX and Regulation CAM, including a new "crypto asset market" category of CFTC-registered exchanges. Unlike the failed Clarity Act, the rules would not force crypto assets onto CFTC-registered platforms, since Chairman Michael Selig said the agency lacks that authority without congressional action. The move follows the Clarity Act's September failure in the Senate, with the SEC and CFTC both pushing ahead on their own rulemaking.

articles.headline: Ethereum Foundation Launches zkAPI for Private API Access
articles.blurb: The Ethereum Foundation released zkAPI, a zero-knowledge protocol that lets users access paid APIs without exposing their identity, counterparty, or consumption patterns to any intermediary. Users deposit ETH into a vault, generate a ZK proof, and receive a fixed quota of API access, with payment metadata abstracted away so no on-chain or off-chain trace links usage back to the caller. OA-chat is live with zkAPI integrated, and the design generalizes to any gated API resource beyond AI inference. Prior unlinkable inference schemes leaked payment trails - zkAPI closes that gap by separating payment metadata from identity at the protocol layer.

articles.headline: Melee Opens Permissionless Market Creation in Phase 2
articles.blurb: Melee bootstrapped 10,000+ price markets and $337.7M in volume over three weeks in Phase 1 by running 5-minute BTC, SOL, and ANSEM rounds 24/7 through its PMM (parimutuel market maker), which pools participant capital and distributes winnings proportionally without requiring external market makers or liquidity incentives. Phase 2 opens market creation to anyone via Melee templates, letting creators claim a market, share it with their audience, and collect fees, with weekly competitions awarding badges to the top markets by volume and unique trader count. The PMM architecture addresses the cold-start liquidity problem that blocks long-tail prediction markets from launching without subsidized counterparties, replacing that dependency with a self-contained pooling mechanism. Creator Score, a reputation layer rating operators by activity, and Phase 3 fully permissionless market creation are next on the roadmap.

articles.headline: SMBC Nikko Building Regulated DeFi Gateway for Japan on Uniswap
articles.blurb: SMBC Nikko and Nethermind are building the DeFi Gateway, a regulated onchain trading venue on Uniswap v4 targeting Japanese investors, with Uniswap Labs, Base, and Nyx Foundation supporting development toward a mid-2027 target. Each pool uses Uniswap v4 hooks to enforce AML/CFT checks and investor protections, embedding Japan's regulatory requirements directly into pool logic. Supported assets span stablecoins, RWAs, and other digital assets, and the pool framework is open for third-party teams to build on. SMBC Nikko and Nethermind will also develop AI-powered vaults and investor onboarding interfaces, with Uniswap Labs advising on integration and liquidity deployment.

articles.headline: Tokenization Was the Easy Part
articles.blurb: Institutional demand for tokenization centers on operational efficiency for familiar assets rather than new asset classes, with clients prioritizing faster settlement, easier venue portability, and collateral utility without forced liquidation. Traditional fund architecture fragments transactions, settlement, and ownership records across separate systems, and moving ownership records onchain consolidates those processes into a single layer. Ethereum Foundation researcher Barnabé Monnot frames this as Ethereum's opening: 100% historical uptime, fast slots and finality arriving via decoupled consensus work, and broad ZK availability replacing multisig trust assumptions together position Ethereum as the global settlement layer.

articles.headline: Fintech is Dead
articles.blurb: Fintech's founding assumptions (mobile-first, cloud-native, and API banking) have become table stakes across all financial services, driving the sector's share of global VC from 14.5% in 2021 to 12.3% in 2025, while the share of fintech capital flowing to AI companies jumped from roughly 10% to 70-80%. The successor architecture runs on two primitives: intelligence tokens and value tokens, joined by a router layer that prices AI inference in deterministic on-chain value millions of times per second. Stripe's $7B acquisition of OpenRouter and Ramp's simultaneous launch of Router.com signal that both operators concluded AI token routing is core financial infrastructure. Downstream, Revolut's PRAGMA model detected 130% more bad credit risk, Figure's tokenized HELOC marketplace cleared $2.8B in quarterly volume at 95% adjusted net-revenue growth, and Robinhood opened 100,000 MCP-enabled agent accounts.

articles.headline: Market Maturation: Crypto Liquid Thoughts, Q4 2026
articles.blurb: The July bottom is confirmed at BTC $59k and ETH $1.6k, and sorts the ensuing bull market opportunity into two buckets: protocols that ARE money (stores of value with uncapped BTC-relative upside) and protocols that MAKE money. For revenue-generating protocols, investors will apply traditional public-market filters, including revenue quality and durability, margin profiles, and institutional access, with the strongest positioning going to projects exposed to RWA and stablecoin growth, backed by founder-CEOs who survived prior bear markets. Onchain AI infrastructure plays (routers, inference, compute, and data) are framed as narrative trades, with specific skepticism around structures where value accrues to equity rather than the token, and a hard run in that category flagged as a potential cycle-top signal.

articles.blurb: Schneider Electric agreed to buy PTC in an all-cash deal valuing its equity at $22.6 billion, with closing expected by Q3 2027 pending approvals. The combination would connect PTC's product design and engineering data with Schneider's operational and energy systems, providing broader context for industrial AI applications.

articles.headline: Reflection unveils 501B-parameter AI model Beam
articles.blurb: Beam is a 501-billion-parameter model that Reflection says competes with leading Chinese models while requiring substantially less compute. Access initially runs through an early-access program, with model weights, documentation, and fine-tuning tools planned for release later this month.

articles.headline: Huawei and Qualcomm Announce Broad Patent License Agreement
articles.blurb: Huawei and Qualcomm announced a multi-year, broad patent license agreement featuring cross-licenses across technology fields including 5G, compute, AI, and networking. Additionally, the agreement includes Qualcomm's purchase of certain Huawei US patents in compute, AI, and networking. The transaction is pending necessary regulatory approvals.

articles.headline: AI productivity needs an organizational redesign
articles.blurb: McKinsey argues that individual productivity gains will struggle to translate into business value unless companies redesign workflows, decision rights, and career paths around human–agent teams. Its proposed approach organizes teams around outcomes, reduces handoffs, and explicitly assigns responsibility for agent actions and the capacity automation frees up.

articles.headline: How Oracle gives AI agents access without handing over control
articles.blurb: Oracle details how it preserves employee permissions across MCP connections and limits coding and operations agents through temporary access, least privilege, and human approval for sensitive actions. The deployment offers a practical example of enforcing authorization in backend systems as assistants move from retrieving information to executing work.

articles.headline: Registered but not routed: what a global audit of IPv6 says about deployment
articles.blurb: Researchers conducted a global audit comparing IPv6 registration records from Regional Internet Registries against live BGP routing tables and the IPv6 Hitlist project. They found that while 92.5 percent of registered IPv6 netblocks appear in live routing, only 79.4 percent of the underlying address space does, revealing a large gap concentrated in unannounced legacy allocations and carrier-grade NAT deployments. Furthermore, cross-checking against the IPv6 Hitlist project identified 28.1 million genuinely distinct, confirmed-live hosts, highlighting a massive amount of unrouted and unmonitored address space worldwide.

articles.headline: Apache Iceberg 1.12.0 Release
articles.blurb: The Apache Iceberg community has announced the release of version 1.12.0, featuring significant performance enhancements, expanded write capabilities for Variant and geospatial data types, and new maintenance tasks. Key updates include faster unshredded Variant reads in Spark, multi-engine shredded Variant writes, and Flink-native resolution of equality deletes into row-position deletion vectors. The release also introduces Hilbert-curve clustering for multi-dimensional sorting, expands REST catalog and OpenAPI protocol features, and lays groundwork for Table Format V4.

articles.headline: ServiceNow Flow Brings a Chat-First Service Desk to Smaller Buyers
articles.blurb: ServiceNow has introduced Flow, an internal startup product offering a chat-first service desk that operates within Slack, Microsoft Teams, and email. Priced at $2 per conversation and $1 per automation run with a $10,000 annual minimum, Flow allows smaller companies and existing customers to bypass traditional portals and ticket forms. Flow's credit card accessibility and public pricing will open ServiceNow to smaller buyers while challenging third-party chat layers built on top of the platform.

articles.headline: Hacking the Go compiler to efficiently map IPv4 to IPv6
articles.blurb: The Go compiler handles mapping IPv4 addresses to IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses inefficiently: the idiomatic netip.AddrFrom16 and As16 pattern runs eight times slower than a native method because of suboptimal compiler optimization. Standard library changes, an unsafe proxy, and custom IR and SSA rewrite rules can eliminate redundant byte-packing and unpacking overhead and achieve native-level performance.

articles.headline: Amazon explores an $8B Nvidia chip sale-leaseback
articles.blurb: Amazon is reportedly discussing a financing arrangement that would sell roughly $8 billion of Nvidia chips into a special-purpose vehicle and lease them back for continued use. The proposal highlights how hyperscalers are seeking outside capital to fund AI expansion while investors take on risks tied to hardware depreciation and future compute demand.

articles.headline: Manage system settings with Endpoint Privilege Management
articles.blurb: Microsoft has documented an Elevation system settings policy for Endpoint Privilege Management in Intune that allows standard users to modify network settings without local administrator rights.

articles.blurb: Namespace raised a $42 million Series B to expand compute infrastructure for coding agents, builds, and testing across Mac, Windows, and Linux.

articles.headline: Dutch Police Arrest ‘Reformed’ Hacker in Shiny Hunters Investigation
articles.blurb: Authorities in the Netherlands have arrested a 23-year-old convicted cybercriminal on suspicion of aiding in data thefts and extortions by the prolific hacker group ShinyHunters. In the days immediately following the suspect's arrest, remaining ShinyHunters members dramatically escalated their attacks, stealing highly sensitive data from the FBI and extorting the Russian ransomware group Cl0p.

articles.headline: U.S. Soldier Gets 70 Months in Prison for AT&T, Verizon Extortions
articles.blurb: A U.S. Army soldier who pleaded guilty to hacking into multiple telecommunications companies and stealing mobile call and text metadata for more than 100 million AT&T customers in 2024 was sentenced to 70 months in federal prison today and ordered to pay nearly $300,000 in restitution to victims.

articles.headline: Data Broker Radaris Loses Domains in Privacy Fight
articles.blurb: The consumer data broker Radaris.com has long had a reputation for ignoring requests to remove personal information from its vast empire of people-search services online. That reputation caught up with the company recently in a lawsuit alleging Radaris violated a New Jersey privacy law that provides for hefty fines against data brokers that publish personal information on state law enforcement officials. In the face of repeated stonewalling and prevarication by attorneys for Radaris, the judge in the case ordered that radaris.com and more than a dozen other data broker domains be transferred to the plaintiffs.

articles.headline: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
articles.blurb: Microsoft Corp. today issued updates to plug at least 974 security holes in its Windows operating systems and other software, by far its biggest single patch batch ever. Microsoft says artificial intelligence is helping to speed the discovery of vulnerabilities, but security experts warn that many organizations already are struggling to prioritize the more human-intensive endeavor of testing and deploying so many fixes each month.

articles.headline: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
articles.blurb: A new identity theft service launched on the dark web this week is selling digital scans of more than 153 million drivers licenses from people in the United States and Canada. Based on interviews with individuals whose licenses are available for purchase on this service, it appears to be siphoning images collected by a widely-used identity verification company based in Louisiana. KrebsOnSecurity also has learned that the New Orleans field office of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) today launched an official inquiry into the source of the images.

articles.headline: Two Alleged ‘TeamPCP’ Hackers Arrested in Australia
articles.blurb: Authorities in Australia have arrested two men believed to be members of TeamPCP, a prolific cybercrime and data extortion group blamed for perpetrating the longest running spree of software supply chain attacks ever. In a statement released today, the Australian Federal Police (AFP) said two unnamed suspects from Western Australia, aged 21 and 23, were arrested in connection with a "sophisticated cybercrime syndicate that allegedly created malicious open-source software to rob thousands of global businesses." The AFP did not name the defendants, but KrebsOnSecurity learned the 21-year-old suspect's real identity in June, and has been communicating with him ever since. This story includes interviews with TeamPCP's self-described spokesperson, and examines clues left behind by the TeamPCP leader that likely led to his undoing.

articles.headline: Who’s Tracking You? Use This New Service to Find Out
articles.blurb: It can be daunting to determine who's responsible for showing ads on the websites we visit, or who's harvesting data from the mobile apps we use every day. That information is already semi-public, but it is not easily parsed and traditionally much of it has remained walled away in the hands of large advertising platforms. Not anymore: A powerful and free new service called DecryptAds scrapes and correlates this adtech data and makes it simple to quickly learn a great deal about the entities that are tracking you.

articles.headline: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 400 Security Holes
articles.blurb: Microsoft today released updates to remedy at least 398 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software, including one weakness that is already being actively exploited and two others that were publicly detailed prior to today.

articles.headline: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions
articles.blurb: A 26-year-old Canadian man once described as one of the most consequential cybercrime threat actors of 2024 has pleaded guilty to computer fraud and conspiracy to hack and extort more than 165 organizations that used the cloud data storage provider Snowflake. Connor Riley Moucka, of Kitchener, Ontario, also admitted to stealing call and text history records of more than 100 million AT&T customers.

articles.headline: Read This Before You Buy That TV Streaming Stick
articles.blurb: Security experts have been sounding the alarm for years about the risks of using generic TV boxes that promise unlimited content streaming for a one-time fee, warning that they secretly rent the user's Internet connection out to strangers. But a groundbreaking new analysis finds these devices also routinely spoof themselves as mobile phones clicking ads on AI-generated websites as part of sprawling operation that seeks to defraud online merchants and advertising networks.

articles.headline: Kenya confirms first Ebola case as virus ‘surges’ in DR Congo province
articles.blurb: Health minister says 28 contacts identified after death of citizen who arrived from DRC on Saturday Kenya has reported its first-ever Ebola death, the health minister announced on Tuesday, as the disease continues to spread rapidly through the north-east of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where the outbreak was announced in May. This is the 17th outbreak of the highly infectious, often deadly disease in the DRC. As of 2 October, 4,082 people had died out of 8,463 confirmed cases in the country since the emergence of the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus, for which there is still no vaccine nor specific treatment.

articles.headline: Tigray rebel groups ‘forcibly recruiting boys as young as 15’ as fighting spreads
articles.blurb: Civilians try to flee as men and boys rounded up on streets by new alliance as Ethiopia conflict erupts again As renewed fighting has threatened a fresh humanitarian crisis in the northern region of Ethiopia, reports are emerging that a new alliance of armed groups in Tigray has been forcibly recruiting men and boys to its ranks. Renewed conflict erupted on 23 September between Ethiopia’s federal government and the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), which rules the region, shattering the fragile Pretoria peace agreement signed between the two sides in November 2022.

articles.headline: Guardian readers fund life-changing surgery for Somali boy injured in US airstrike
articles.blurb: After Guardian investigation uncovered drone strike that killed 12 civilians and injured many more, seven-year-old Abdiqadir Salah underwent vital operation in Mogadishu On the rickshaw ride to the hospital, Marian Haji Abdi Guled felt a mixture of joy and apprehension: the day they had been waiting for had finally arrived. Almost a year earlier, her then seven-year-old son, Abdiqadir Salah, had been seriously injured, alongside his two siblings, in what a Guardian investigation found was a US drone strike on the village of Jamaame in Somalia that killed at least 12 civilians, including eight children.

articles.headline: Skull fractures suggest servants of Egypt’s ancient kings were sacrificed
articles.blurb: Study of remains taken from royal cemetery at Umm el-Qa’ab appears to confirm early Egyptologist’s theory Court officials and craftspeople serving early Egyptian kings may have been sacrificed when their ruler died, according to research that found fractures in several ancient skulls. The royal cemetery of Umm el-Qa’ab near Abydos features the tombs and enclosures of the First Dynasty rulers of Egypt, and dates as far back as 3,000BC.

articles.headline: Egyptian journalist faces terrorism charges after entire newsroom detained
articles.blurb: Calls for release of six Matsadaash staff after one is charged, while whereabouts of other five remain unknown An Egyptian journalist has been charged with joining a terrorist group, days after an entire newsroom was detained in what rights groups have said is a crackdown on press freedoms. Last week, authorities arrested six journalists from the independent fact-checking and investigative platform Matsadaash – literally meaning “don’t believe” – accusing them in a statement of being unlicensed and publishing false news on behalf of the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood.

articles.headline: US man arrested as second suspect in Canada mass school shooting planned with ChatGPT
articles.blurb: Justice department detained James Codey Bryant and allege he offered ‘technical advice’ to primary suspect A surprise suspected accomplice has been arrested in connection with a mass school shooting in Canada that was made notorious after an 18-year-old allegedly killed six children after discussing it with the AI chatbot ChatGPT. The US Department of Justice said Tuesday it had detained James Codey Bryant, 30, a resident of western Washington state, on a charge of conspiracy to murder persons in a foreign country.

articles.headline: Outcry in Trinidad and Tobago after passing of police bill that could threaten press freedom
articles.blurb: Journalists call for urgent amendment to special operations bill, which increases police search and seizure powers Journalists in Trinidad and Tobago have called for an urgent amendment to a sweeping new bill that increases police powers of search and seizure, which they argue threatens the country’s much-vaunted freedom of the press. The government says the special operations bill 2026, passed on 24 September, is designed to tackle alarmingly high crime and murder rates in the Caribbean nation.

articles.headline: Argentina will stop Falklands exploiting offshore oilfields, foreign minister says
articles.blurb: Pablo Quirno says move is part of Argentinian government’s strategy to peacefully assert sovereignty over the islands Argentina’s foreign minister has told an audience that included the British ambassador that his government would stop the Falkland Islands from exploiting its offshore oilfields as part of a strategy to take sovereignty. During a speech at a thinktank event in the Argentinian capital, Pablo Quirno condemned the British government for failing to open negotiations over the islands and facilitating a significant offshore oil project in its waters.

articles.headline: Flávio’s surprise first-round election win highlights rapid rise of Brazil’s House of Bolsonaro
articles.blurb: Four members of disgraced ex-president Jair Bolsonaro’s family have been elected to office, most notably his wife and son Flávio, who won the first round of voting to be Brazil’s new president The weekend’s elections in Brazil not only put Jair Bolsonaro’s eldest son, Flávio Bolsonaro, in the lead in the presidential race, but also underscored how far the former president has come in building a political dynasty. As his far-right senator son heads into a runoff against the leftist incumbent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, a sweeping far-right victory in congressional races also secured seats for Jair Bolsonaro’s wife, two of his sons and one of his brothers.

articles.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro poised to win Brazilian presidency after shock first-round victory
articles.blurb: Progressive voters and supporters of incumbent president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva left reeling after far-right surge Flávio Bolsonaro is in pole position to win Brazil’s presidential election, after a far-right tsunami propelled him to a shock first-round victory over the incumbent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, leaving progressive voters reeling. The 45-year-old rightwing candidate received 56.1m votes to Lula’s 53.8m – 47.03% to 45.16% – meaning the 80-year-old leftwinger has a mountain to climb if he is to bounce back in the second round on 25 October. Never, since the return of democracy to Brazil in 1985, has the first-round runner-up managed to turn the game around and win the second ballot.

articles.headline: EU negotiators head to China hoping to curb cheap imports of hybrid electric cars
articles.blurb: Mood in trade talks said to have changed as EU member states harden demands for protection against Chinese imports EU trade negotiators are heading to China for two days of crunch talks aimed at sealing a breakthrough deal tackling Beijing’s record £1bn-a-day trade surplus by curbing its exports of cheap hybrid electric cars into Europe. Trade commissioner Maroš Šefčovič and his team fly out on Wednesday and will be negotiating up to the wire in talks scheduled to start the following day and continue late into Friday.
